newsitem.title: USA: Republicans say budget accord laid out by leaders.
newsitem.headline: Republicans say budget accord laid out by leaders.

text.p: Republican lawmakers said party leaders presented a "budget accord" to a closed caucus Thursday and a final agreement with the White House was expected to be reached later in the day.
Rep. Marge Roukema, Rep-N.J., told reporters House Speaker Newt Gingrich and Budget Committee Chairman John Kasich "indicated that it should be finalized this afternoon."
Roukema said, "It seems as though there is an enormous amount of agreement across the board on the budget."

Republican sources said the budget would include a five-year gross tax cut of $135 billion. Medicare spending would be reduced by $115 billion over the five years. The budget accord is designed to bring the federal deficit to zero by 2002.

Republicans and conservative Democrats, known as Blue Dogs, scheduled a joint news conference for 2 P.M.EDT (1800 GMT). Republican Whip Tom Delay of Texas said he expected that conservative Democrats would support the package. The closed-door Republican conference erupted into cheers when party leaders concluded their presentation of the budget accord reached with President Bill Clinton.
